headline:
Partly, and not where you suspected. The tier structure is sound: quick on push, full on release, and a cheap release-boundary job (about 20 s of runner time, no wall time). I found no layers that duplicate each other's assertions, so do not cut layers. What is slow is one selection rule and a few implementation defects.

1. Your local 10+ minutes is real, not machine load. The merge agent's 569 s run reproduces at idle. 78% of it (445 of 569 s) is suites picked only because file names collide (SPEC.md, frames/plan.txt, frames/review.txt). The biggest, shiploop-e2e, is 322 s of it because a 2 s poll sleep waits on fake hosts that exit at once. A 4-line patch took it from 322 s to 58 s with every test passing. Five release-file suites at the release commit add about 66 s [I], which fits your 10+ minutes.
2. GitHub quick got slower: median 2m35s before 10-03 22:21Z, 4m24s since, worst 11m31s, because that same suite is selected in 12 of 16 recent runs.
3. Full tier on release: median 18m39s, held up by two single processes (plan-dispatcher-mutants about 10 min, the E2E apparatus 10 to 19 min). Under your proceed-optimistically rule you do not wait on it.

The real design tax is pins (22 of 36 red runs since 09-22), not CI minutes.

First: the poll fix with a test, then the name collisions (an explicit path for the real SPEC.md, not blanket generic stems), then print per-suite seconds.
timings:
Source reliability: GitHub job data (60 runs, per job) is the most precise. Local numbers carry a macOS spawn multiplier, so use GitHub or CPU figures for CI claims.

WAIT 1, quick tier on GitHub. There are two regimes, and the draft's single median hid that.
- Last 100 runs (79 quick): median 155 s [M, my gh run list recompute]. Before 10-03T22:21Z (61 runs, e2e at 8 to 12 s): median 150 s. Since then (18 runs): median 264 s (4m24s), p-max 691 s (11m31s) [M]. Sorted post-cut walls: 112, 138, 146, 150, 230 to 307 (11 runs), 402, 456, 461, 691.
- 12 of the 16 post-cut runs in my data set (and 14 of 18 per the attack) select shiploop-e2e [M, quick_runs.json]; 27 of 31 pre-cut did too.
- Worst run 37333343558 (33 suites): 691 s wall; e2e 303.0 s of a 634 s test step, the other 31 suites about 320 s [M, log]. Run 37335808254 (17 suites): 456 s, e2e 301.9 s [M, attack's log read].
- Non-test overhead (checkout, setup, plan, aggregate, handoffs) is 46 to 48 s median; release-boundary (about 20 s) runs parallel to plan and adds 0 s of wall [M]. Queue 2 s median. 8 of 100 recent runs failed (all on 09-27, 09-28, 10-03) [M].

WAIT 2, full tier on a release commit: median 18m39s over 13 releases (range 17m45s to 19m38s); 18m42s over the 21 full runs in the last 100 [M]. Critical path: plan 14 s, then the slowest job about 18m12s, then 3 s. Core gates 9 of 13, e2e-apparatus 4 of 13, shiploop shards never. Core is about 18 min, of which plan-dispatcher-mutants is 435 to 644 s (635.6 s latest) [M: it is the only core Python suite with 2 test methods, and 'Ran 2 tests in 435 to 644 s' appears in all 13 core logs]. The apparatus is bimodal (590 to 782 s in 6 runs, 1040 to 1135 s in 7) against a 1200 s suite timeout (about 5% margin in slow mode). A release costs about 57.7 job-min vs about 3.4 for a quick push; full is 22% of runs and 82% of runner minutes. 0 of 13 recent full runs failed.

WAIT 3, local quick tier. Receipt: the merge agent's rel2 run, 569.0 s, 28 suites, 103 changed paths vs origin/main [M]. quick() at origin/main a9f592a3 over those 103 paths returns exactly those 28 suites [M, I ran it]. Shares, disjoint: false-positive suites 444.6 s (78.1%: shiploop-e2e 322.3, 8 plan-dispatcher-* suites 109.2, shiploop-run-review 7.7, review-coverage 5.4); the 16-suite fixed baseline 124.1 s (21.8%, includes test-groups 2.0 s); footprint-only suites 0.2 s (rubric-eval). The draft's 78/22/0.4 summed to 100.4% because test-groups was counted twice. Idle reproduction: e2e 322.1 s (receipt 322.3), chain-async 83.5 s (receipt 83.5), at load 3.4 to 6.5 [M, attack's files, outputs re-read]. Idle macOS-vs-GitHub multipliers: chain-async 83.5 vs 34.5 s (2.4x), chain-git 149.1 vs 25.2 s (5.9x), workspace 131.0 vs 26.4 s (5.0x), with sys time above user time in the last two [M]. Load (6 to 62 on 18 cores) inflated other lanes' serial baselines, not this receipt. The receipt is at 192c1e69; the release commit 520bfb85 selects five more suites (release-flow 31.9, native-marketplace-adapters 21.8, marketplace-package 4.5, marketplace-host-isolation 6.3, marketplace-run 1.7 = 66.3 s) so 569.0 + 66.3 = 635 s, about 10m35s [I: assumes the owner ran at the release HEAD].
why_slow:
1. Over-selection by name collision [M]. quick() matches changed files to suites by file name (the stem rule and _referencing in test/suite_catalog.py). Collisions: every skills/*/SPEC.md and every experiment-fixture SPEC.md selects shiploop-e2e and shiploop-run-review because their sources mention test/shiploop_e2e/SPEC.md (20 of 22 files with stem 'spec' are collisions; only test/shiploop_e2e/SPEC.md has a real reader). Any file stemmed 'plan' selects all 8 plan-dispatcher-* suites (16 of 16 such files; none has a real reader: they are rubric-eval frames, frozen evidence). 'review' selects review-coverage (8 files, all rubric-eval frames, evidence, or test/shiploop_e2e/review.py). Of the 28 selected suites in the rel2 case, 11 are false positives (445 s), 16 are the fixed baseline. Replaying the corrected rule (plan, review, spec generic + one explicit path for the real SPEC.md) over the 103 receipt paths gives 17 suites and 124.4 s of the receipt's time [M, my replay].

2. A stale hand-kept duration table [M]. _DURATION_SECONDS lists shiploop-e2e at 0.7 s (written at 14 tests); it now has 224 to 225 tests and takes 303 s on GitHub. The 120 s 'light' filter treats a missing entry as 0.0 s; 46 of 108 suites have no entry (62 have one) at a9f592a3. The only guard, test_quick_never_runs_heavy_suites_or_the_apparatus, checks the table against itself, so it passed while the entry was wrong by 430x.

3. Slow suites are mostly implementation defects, each measured, none applied:
- shiploop-e2e: about 290 s of 322 s is time.sleep(2) in run.launch() (test/shiploop_e2e/run.py, the poll loop) polling fake hosts that exit in under a second. Replacing it with proc.wait(timeout=2) gave 322.1 s to 58.3 s with 225 of 225 passing at idle [M, attack's run, outputs and diff re-read]; the first lane measured 329.3 to 72.6 s under load.
- Apparatus (338 tests): 402.5 s of 467 s is in-process CPU (92,279 re.search calls under freeze_package, via _sanitize_text(decoded) != decoded). A 7-line memo took 467.2 s to 103.4 s with 338 of 338 passing [M, profile lane]. I confirmed the check is a pure function of the file bytes (sha256 verified first, a fresh sanitizer per call).
- plan-dispatcher-mutants: 38 mutants each rerun a whole node suite; the model gives 639 s vs 635.6 s measured. Each mutant names its killed_by scenario; a single-scenario run of the 10 scenario mutants took 51 s wall and killed 10 of 10 (that file only).
- Chain family: each shiploop CLI call spawns about 54 children; _assert_no_active_operation runs 8 git rev-parse per target_identity call. A batched rev-parse cut chain-git spawns 30.5% and chain-async wall 26% (lifecycle, chain and native-pilot not run).
- Not the cause: fixture cost (git init 0.02 to 0.09 s; package build about 23 s per full tier; no real network).

4. Fixed baseline. 16 suites always run (12 ShipLoop). On the idle receipt they sum to 124.1 s, of which chain-async is 83.5 s (67%); the other 15 sum to 40.6 s. A docs-only push is 112 to 150 s on GitHub post-cut.

5. The release full tier has two independent long poles (mutants about 10 min in core, the apparatus 10 to 19 min). Moving mutants to its own job moves the median only 1119 s to 1091 s [M]. The wall changes materially only if both are cut: about 10.5 to 11 min [I, at the draft's ratios, not measured on GitHub].

6. Local-only multiplier: spawn-bound suites run 2.4 to 5.9x slower on the Mac than on the runner at idle (sys time at or above user time); sleep-bound ones match (e2e 322 s vs 303 s). The local run also selects from the whole diff vs origin/main (103 files here); a GitHub push selects from before..HEAD (median 2 files).
value_evidence:
Failures lane (331 runs since 08-01, 70 red logs read), re-read against the attacks.

Caught real regressions [M]: since 09-22, 4 of 16 breakages (25%), 9 of 36 red runs: shiploop-navigator-contract (a refused retired run still written to; a locator count that only CI's short temp path exposed), installed-skill-invocation (CLI error prefix lost, caught only by the full tier), shiploop-mock-replay (package fingerprint). All 8 quick failures in the last 100 runs were caught by selected suites.

Broke only on legitimate change (pins) [M]: 22 of 36 red runs and 9 of 16 breakages since 09-22. Families: the test-groups count pin (7 red runs, 3 breakages; 36 count-bump commits since 07-27), navigator and improve-schedule wording, chain/quality/ui-allocation fixtures after an intended contract change, native-pilot 'protocol 3' (fixed by reading PROTOCOL_VERSION), no-model-launch denylist, apparatus verb allowlist and trace-corpus hash pin, install-targets layout. About 13 repair commits of 449; median 35 min first red to next green. 20 of 36 red runs were pushes onto an already-red main. About 7.5% of Python test methods (151 of 2,023) are pure text pins.

Quick-tier catches: of 12 red quick runs, 9 came from the fixed baseline, 3 from a directly changed suite or the e2e prefix, 0 from the name-stem, reference or hub heuristics. Qualification: those 9 are runs, not breakages. Counting carry-overs on an already-red main once, the attack puts it at about 5 distinct breakages, all with ShipLoop-path diffs except test-groups (approximate; I did not re-derive it). A selected suite that passed is invisible, so '0 from heuristics' means never seen to catch, not worthless.

Never failed [M]: 96 of 106 suites in the last 150 runs. Limits: zero failures cannot show a suite is useless; local pre-push catches are invisible; the 'time in zero-failure suites' figure uses stale durations. Mutation evidence runs the other way for the chain suites (removing the stale-attempt guard failed 3 lifecycle tests and no other suite), so lifecycle's silence is not redundancy. plan-dispatcher-mutants is a test of tests by design.

Full tier on release [M]: 3 full-only incidents, all within 28 hours of the 09-26 tier change, all pin, fixture or layout class except installed-skill-invocation. 23 consecutive green full runs since; whether that is steady state is unknown.

Five senses of over-design:
(a) Too many suites for the footprint: PARTLY. Engine-file selection is accurate (28 of 31 traced suites opened a changed file). The excess is the name collisions (445 of 569 s) and the stale duration table. The e2e directory-prefix excess is small: only 7 of 159 commits touching test/shiploop_e2e/ since 09-26 touch no code file (3 baselines.jsonl, which the e2e source names; 4 evidence/*.json, which run-review reads) [M, my git log]. One real narrowness: native-pilot (experiments-shiploop-chain-native-pilot, 72.5 s, light) is not selected by edits to shiploop_protocol.py, shiploop_navigator.py or shiploop_chain.py [M, I ran targeted()]; the fixed 9-suite hub set cuts the rest. That is the shape of the 09-24 miss.
(b) Suites that police themselves: cheap in seconds (test-groups 2.0 s, ci-policy 2.4 s), costly in churn (110 commits since 07-27 touched policing files).
(c) Pins that break on legitimate change: YES, the clearest over-design. Cost is repair time and red noise, not CI minutes.
(d) Layers that duplicate each other: NOT SUPPORTED. 3.6% of 1,526 asserted literals appear in 2 or more files; 22 of 30 sampled tests were sole guards; one of 5 mutations was killed by 13 suites. n is small; JS, shell, ask-agent and improve were not traced.
(e) Slow suites that could be shared-fixture fast: NO. They are defects: a poll tick, a regex scan, spawn counts, mutant reruns.

options.option: Fix the 2-second poll tick in shiploop-e2e (test/shiploop_e2e/run.py, launch(): replace time.sleep(2) with proc.wait(timeout=2), ignoring TimeoutExpired; deadline and stop_when checks unchanged). Add a deterministic regression test in the existing test/shiploop-e2e.test.py: launch an immediately exiting fake host with run.time.sleep patched to count calls and assert zero. This is the missing guard: nothing script-run catches this defect class today.
options.saves: Idle local 322.1 s to 58.3 s with 225 of 225 passing [M, attack's run]. GitHub about 303 s to about 60 to 67 s [I]. Applies to 12 of 16 post-cut quick runs. Alone it takes the rel2 receipt from about 569 s to about 305 s locally [I]; the worst GitHub run (691 s) to about 455 s [I], so O3 and O4 are not optional for wide diffs.
options.risk: Low. About 26 s of sleep remains in tests that deliberately hang a fake host until --timeout. Real hour-long E2E runs use the same launch(), but the deadline logic is unchanged.
options.evidence_needed: 225 of 225 locally with the patch; the 'Ran N tests in X s' line from the next GitHub quick run that selects e2e; the new test failing on the old loop.

options.option: After O1 lands, re-record shiploop-e2e's _DURATION_SECONDS entry from the GitHub 'Ran N tests in X s' line (about 60 to 70 s), so the light filter and shard assignment are truthful and e2e stays in quick.
options.saves: No direct seconds; stops the slowest quick suite being filed at 0.7 s.
options.risk: Order matters. Recording the current 303 s without O1 would drop e2e from every ordinary quick push, and its catches (3 red quick runs in the last 150) would wait for release. Use GitHub seconds, never local ones.

options.option: Stop file names selecting unrelated suites, in three explicit moves. (a) Add 'plan', 'review' and 'spec' to _GENERIC_STEMS in test/suite_catalog.py (every file with those stems is a rubric-eval frame, frozen evidence, or test/shiploop_e2e/review.py; rubric-eval is still selected by its leaf rule). (b) Because 'spec' also removes the one real reader link, add test/shiploop_e2e/SPEC.md to _PATH_SUITE_IDS mapping to (shiploop-e2e, shiploop-run-review): run-review asserts every S-n clause its defaults name exists in that file, e2e and navigator-contract read it, 17 of 399 non-merge commits since 09-26 edit it. (c) Optional: fix the single index.html collision (skills/shiploop-run-review/template/index.html selecting serve-fixture) with a path-scoped exclusion, not by making 'index' generic, which would stop browser_consumer/*/index.html selecting serve-fixture. DROPPED from the draft: the 'repo-relative tail when a basename is shared' rule (suites reference files by pathlib joins, so a literal-tail match finds almost no real readers and the rule was undefined) and the narrowing of the test/shiploop_e2e/ prefix (7 of 159 commits).
options.saves: rel2 case: 28 suites and 569 s to 17 suites and 124.4 s of the receipt's time [M, my replay over the 103 receipt paths]. Removes the 8 plan-dispatcher suites (109 s), e2e and run-review (330 s) and review-coverage (5 s) from collision cases.
options.risk: Under-selection. A red-history replay cannot show true positives stay (a selected suite that passed is invisible, and every dropped suite in a replay was never red). Verify by (1) a must-select / must-not-select table asserted in the existing test/test-groups.test.py (SPEC.md under test/shiploop_e2e selects e2e and run-review; local-candidate/index.html selects serve-fixture; skills/rubric-eval/SPEC.md, frames/plan.txt and frames/review.txt select none of e2e, run-review, plan-dispatcher-*, review-coverage), not a new top-level suite (that bumps the 108-suite count pin); (2) an audit-hook trace of every (path, suite) pair the replay drops, confirming the suite never opens the path.
options.evidence_needed: The table passing; the trace output. The 1411d5f1 probe discrepancy is settled and needs no further check: quick() at origin/main reproduces the receipt's 28 suites exactly, and the probe lacked the colliding file names.

options.option: Make per-suite time visible: print 'OK <id> (<s>s)' with flush in test/run_suites.py and write a sorted table to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY; emit a WARN line (not a failure, which would be another pin-style red cause) when a quick-selected suite's measured seconds exceed QUICK_MAX_SECONDS. Refresh the 46 missing and the stale _DURATION_SECONDS entries from GitHub run logs or GitHub receipts only, never local runs; leave node and bash suites that GitHub cannot time unset. Fix the README claims (suites over two minutes never run in quick; the hub selects 'every light ShipLoop suite') and release checklist step 3.
options.saves: No seconds directly; removes the blind spot (three audit lanes could not read per-suite GitHub time because stdout is block-buffered and 626 receipt artifacts go unread).

options.option: Memoize the apparatus credential-shape check (_sanitize_text(decoded) != decoded in freeze_package) by file-content hash. Preferred variant: build the cache inside the test fixture so no shipped security code changes. If it goes into skills/shiploop-e2e-audit/harness/run.py, it needs a changes/shiploop-e2e-audit/*.md note (LEAF_SOURCE in scripts/check-release-boundary.py matches skills/<leaf>/) or a 'No-Change-Note: test-only speedup' trailer, and the key should include the sanitizer identity so a future test that patches the sanitizer cannot get a stale answer.
options.saves: Local 467.2 s to 103.4 s with 338 of 338 passing [M, profile lane]; GitHub 766 s to about 170 s [I]. Removes the bimodal 590 to 1135 s spread and the 5% margin under the 1200 s timeout.

options.evidence_needed: A reviewer confirming purity for the chosen variant; one GitHub full run.

options.option: Run each mutant in plan-dispatcher-mutants against only its named killed_by scenario (mutate.py passes the scenario id when the mutants file sets scenario_argument). Keep the full baseline run and add a baseline pass of each distinct killed_by scenario run alone against the unmutated package.

options.evidence_needed: Run all 38 mutants both ways, compare killed sets, record in the journal; confirm decisions and exact-calls mutants are unchanged.

The idle numbers: the 15 baseline suites other than chain-async sum to 40.6 s serial, so 2 workers can save at most about half of that; the floor is the longest suite (chain-async 83.5 s locally; e2e about 58 s after O1). The draft's '104.2 s to 26.2 s' pair was taken under load 8 to 33 and is withdrawn (a 4x gain from 2 workers is not possible).

recommendation:
Do these in order, each as its own verified increment. Add a change note wherever a file under skills/<leaf>/ is touched (the release-boundary job fails CI without one, or a No-Change-Note trailer): that covers O5 if done in the harness, and O7. O1 to O4 touch test files only.

1. O1 with its regression test. Verify all tests locally, then read the 'Ran N tests in X s' line on the next GitHub quick run that selects e2e (expect about 303 s to about 60 to 67 s). Then O2, from that GitHub number only.
2. O3 as corrected: three stems plus one explicit SPEC.md path (optional index.html scope). Verify with the must-select / must-not-select table in test/test-groups.test.py and the audit-hook trace of every dropped (path, suite) pair, not with a red-history replay. Expect the rel2 case at 17 suites and about 124 s locally (simulated [M]); O1 plus O3 together take the receipt from 569 s to about 124 s [I from measured parts].
3. O4: per-suite seconds, a WARN on quick-selected suites over the cutoff, GitHub-sourced durations only.
4. O11 minimal (native-pilot) and O10. They are coverage and red-noise items under your own rules, not wait items, so do not gate them on a measured wait.
5. O5 and O6 together, because the release tier has two long poles. Verify on the next release run's job times (core about 18 min to about 10 min; apparatus 10 to 19 min to about 3 min); release wall about 18.7 min to about 10.5 to 11 min [I].
6. Stop and re-decide. O7 to O9, O12 and O13 only if a measured wait still hurts.

For wide, merge-sized or docs-and-skills diffs, the local quick tier is not the check. By your own rule CI on main is, and you do not wait on it; release checklist step 3 currently points at the run that cost you the 10 minutes.

DO NOT TOUCH:
- The release-boundary job (about 20 s, off the critical path).
- The fixed baseline, until the O9 diff check says which pushes it caught.
- shiploop-chain, chain-lifecycle and the other chain suites (mutation tests show lifecycle is the only guard for two chain branches).
- The navigator door suites (each caught something unique).
- The plan-dispatcher-mutants gate itself: speed it up, do not remove it.
- The E2E harness and apparatus tooling suites (14 of 17 sampled were sole guards; your 09-24 misses were this kind).
- The full-on-release policy and the fail-closed aggregate, plan and guard jobs.
- The catalog_omissions registry guard.
- The drift guards (hash pin, CLI-verb allowlist): keep them, but prefer derive, don't pin when touching them.
unknowns: REJECTED: the attack's request to treat the capture.py feed/_next_prefix rescan as 'the real cost in the security code' and queue a follow-up. It is unmeasured (the overlap lane named it without a patch), while the memo alone removed 364 of the 467 s in the profile lane's run. Kept as an unverified lead, not a commitment.

REJECTED: the draft's own 'repo-relative tail when a basename is shared' rule and its narrowing of the test/shiploop_e2e/ prefix. Rejected after the attack, with evidence: suites reference files by pathlib joins (shiploop-e2e.test.py:828, shiploop-navigator-contract.test.py:2655), and only 7 of 159 commits touch no code file under that prefix. This is an acceptance of the attack, listed so it is not mistaken for a surviving claim.

REJECTED: the draft's 'tier structure and the cheap release-boundary job add about 48 s' and its 'quick: that is fine / worst 7m41s'. The 46 to 48 s is total non-test wall; release-boundary adds 0 s of wall; and the current quick regime is 4m24s median, 11m31s worst. Accepted from the attack and re-derived from gh run list.

Your own local run over 10 minutes was not measured; the receipt is the merge agent's rel2 run (569 s at 192c1e69, 9m30s). That the release HEAD adds about 66 s of marketplace and release suites is inferred from catalog path rules and the core receipt's per-suite times, not measured as a run.

No GitHub measurement exists for any proposed fix. GitHub savings are ratio estimates from local measurements; the e2e idle patch run (322 to 58 s, 225 of 225) was run by an attack lane and I re-read its output and diff but did not re-run it. The 08-gate numbers for chain-git and workspace multipliers likewise rest on that lane's files.
Per-suite GitHub times for node and bash suites: stdout is block-buffered; the hermetic-<group> receipt.json artifacts would settle it but need your approval to download.
Why the E2E apparatus is bimodal on GitHub (590 to 782 s vs 1040 to 1135 s): not region or runner image; the runner CPU model is not in the logs. A CPU-bound cause is plausible [I].
